solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get backache supporting power plant

indicators.note: supporting means holding up from below, so the backache comes after the power letter

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: Someone tells you that a power station will give you a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' properly suits a down clue (one piece under another); in this across clue it just means LUMBAGO follows P. 'Get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is a flowering shrub, also called leadwort, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: 5 = 51 +10 / 1 (back in France)

indicators.note: the slash is read as a dividing line with the other piece inside it, so it works as a container

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
X is 10 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: back says the French word for one is turned round

parts.note: one in French is un, as the bracketed in France tells you

explanation.surface: It looks like an arithmetic sum with a French footnote rather than a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition '5' points to 5 Down, OPERATING SYSTEM. 'in France' makes the 1 French; 'back' turns that word round, and the slash, read as a dividing line, holds it inside the two numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Linux is a free computer platform that runs machines, an example of the kind of software at 5 Down.

clue.text: Curriculum is in form educators admitted was in error

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the letters sit inside the phrase curriculum is in form educators

explanation.surface: A school syllabus brought in by teachers turned out to be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the M at the end of 'Curriculum' and ends with the ED at the start of 'educators'. 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given wrong information is mistaken, so the adjective means in error.

clue.text: Not sure article was written by early Christian philosopher

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the Gnostics were an early Christian sect who claimed secret spiritual knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure whether a piece of writing was by an early Church thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that God's existence cannot be known, so is doubtful rather than believing.

clue.text: Maintains it in working order?

parts.note: read it as IT, information technology: the software that keeps computers running, which is also a working (operating) order (system)

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a machine running smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is dropped from IT, so 'it' looks like a pronoun; the question mark flags the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The core software of a computer runs and manages the hardware, keeping information technology going.

clue.text: People take both sides before one magician

indicators.note: take means the people word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: before puts the two side letters ahead of the one

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, the two sides
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Folk pick sides before turning to a single conjurer.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlin is the wizard of Arthurian legend, the best-known magician of British myth.

clue.text: Jam is contaminated by radioactive metal strip

parts.note: a jam of people is a crowd or mob

indicators.note: contaminated by means the uranium symbol gets into the word is

parts.note: taken as written
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Preserves are polluted by a strip of radioactive metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radioactive metal strip' reads as one phrase, but the metal is U and 'strip' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Möbius strip is a band with a half twist giving it only one side, so this names a kind of strip.

clue.text: Balderdash — right about nothing!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the right abbreviation goes round the nothing

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a claim that is right about nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot is informal for nonsense, the same as balderdash.

clue.text: Unfair to bail queen out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: It would be unjust to post bail for the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequable means uneven or not equal, so unfair in its treatment.

clue.text: Where students are working in this together

parts.note: unis is short for universities, where students study
on means working, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: In their colleges, students are all working together.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase with the answer standing in for 'this': in unison means together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in unison is doing it all at once as one, which is acting together.

clue.text: It takes time to cut ash into incense

indicators.note: to cut means the other letters slice into the ash word

parts.note: an ember is a glowing fragment left in the ash of a fire
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cuts ash to make sweet-smelling joss sticks, given time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' looks like the burning perfume, which fits the ash, but it is the verb meaning to make angry. 'takes' joins IT and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them angry and resentful, which is what embitter means too.

clue.text: Some nerve to have weapon attached!

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of axe, a weapon
on means attached, as in a lid on a jar

explanation.surface: It takes some cheek to turn up carrying an axe!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some nerve' sounds like a remark about cheek; it means part of a nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: An axon is the long fibre of a nerve cell carrying impulses, so it is part of a nerve.

clue.text: August sees trains swapping halves in front immediately

indicators.note: in front places the medical word before the rest

parts.note: stat is medical shorthand for immediately

indicators.note: swapping halves means the second half of the word is moved ahead of the first

parts.note: queues are lines or trains of people

explanation.surface: In August, railway carriages are rearranged at the front straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: August with a capital looks like the month, but it is the adjective meaning grand. 'swapping halves' moves the back half of the trains word to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuesque means tall, dignified and imposing like a statue, which is the august, stately quality.

clue.text: One gray sunlit explosion might be found at the centre of a black hole

definitions.text: might be found at the centre of a black hole

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single grey sunlit blast could sit at the heart of a black hole.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics a singularity is a point of infinite density, which theory places at the core of a black hole.

clue.text: In Bristol, I unearthed cones

indicators.note: unearthed means dug up, so the letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone digs up pine cones in Bristol, the English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Strobili is the botanical plural for the cone-shaped fruiting bodies of conifers.

clue.text: Cases to insulate edges in brew?

definitions.text: Cases to insulate edges in brew?

indicators.note: in brew means the letters are stirred up together
edges means the outside letters of the word insulate

explanation.surface: Covers that keep the pot warm sit around the tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay; 'insulate' gives only its edges, I and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea cosies are padded covers put over teapots to keep the brew hot.

clue.text: Snatches an unknown number of sailors

parts.note: N stands for an unknown number in algebra
ABs are able seamen, sailors

explanation.surface: Press gangs grab who knows how many seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab is to grab or seize, so nabs means snatches.

clue.text: Forms of address written on some paper in letter

indicators.note: in means the paper word goes inside the letter's name

parts.note: ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S
a quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: Polite titles are written on a sheet of a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like correspondence, but it is a letter of the alphabet written out.
explanation.definitionFit: Esquire is a courtesy title written after a man's name, so the plural names forms of address.

clue.text: Obscure tree

definitions.meaning: to hide it in the hand, concealing it from view
a tall tropical tree with a crown of large leaves

explanation.definitionFit: Palming conceals a thing, and the palm is also a familiar tropical tree.

clue.text: Movements of tailless birds had raised tracks

indicators.note: had means held, so the birds word holds the tracks inside it
tailless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: geese are birds

indicators.note: raised means turned upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ruts are tracks worn into the ground

explanation.surface: Birds with no tails left raised tracks as they moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' (STUR from RUTS) suits a down clue; here it just means reversed. GEES, from GEESE, holds STUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestures are movements of the hands or body made to express something.

clue.text: Book is gross

definitions.meaning: a single bound book, especially one of a set
the whole bulk or total amount of something

explanation.definitionFit: A volume is one book of a series, and also the total quantity or bulk, the gross amount.

clue.text: Congratulations on being healthy!

definitions.meaning: the phrase said to praise someone on an achievement
describing food or exercise that benefits you

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of praise and also describes anything wholesome or beneficial.

clue.text: Missing man weary of hiding odd characters

indicators.note: hiding odd characters means the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of man weary are concealed, leaving only the even ones

explanation.surface: A tired man has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is away is absent, not present, which is missing.

clue.text: Fruit found in a cereal

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A fruit turns up in a bowl of breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak, botanically its fruit.

clue.text: Throw off dogma — don't go around holding on to what is acceptable

indicators.note: holding means the result keeps another letter inside
go around means the word don't surrounds the dogma

parts.note: taken as written without its apostrophe
an ism is a doctrine or dogma
U means socially acceptable, upper-class, in the old British U and non-U usage

explanation.surface: Someone urges you to shake off doctrine, not dodging it but clinging to what is proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go around' wraps the doctrine in the first gap of DON'T and 'holding' adds U in the second; the apostrophe is ignored and 'on to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that throws off its rider makes the rider dismount, the transitive sense of the verb.

clue.text: Going up river in waterproof

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: Going upriver calls for a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac, short for mackintosh, is a waterproof raincoat.

clue.text: Is horn fixed on these?

indicators.note: fixed means put right or rearranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a horn is attached to certain animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is definition and wordplay at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoceroses carry a horn on the snout, so they are what a horn is fixed on.

clue.text: Steel oneself to take drug revealing inner spirit

parts.note: to psych yourself up is to steel yourself
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone braces themselves and takes a drug to reveal their soul.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek thought the psyche is the soul or mind, a person's inner spirit.

clue.text: Rambling prophet almost good to retain philosophical principle

indicators.note: to retain means the outer letters keep the principle inside them
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Moses is the Old Testament prophet
yin is the passive principle of Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A wandering prophet nearly manages to keep hold of a philosophical idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To mosey is to stroll in a leisurely way, so moseying is rambling.
